# Module `regex`

regex - POSIX extended regular expressions over String bytes.

Thin wrappers over the runtime's `__vyb_regex_*` functions in
`runtime/vyb_runtime.c`. Matching and the offsets returned by `regex_find` are
byte-based, in line with the Vyb String model, so providers parsing HTML/URL
text can rely on the same indices as the rest of the stdlib.

Fallible lookups follow the engine-wide `T?` shape (PROGRAMMERS_GUIDE §3.16):
`regex_find` returns `Int?` (absent when there is no match, so a match at byte
offset 0 is unambiguous) and `regex_capture_match` / `regex_capture` return
`String?` (absent when the pattern does not match, present holding the captured
text -- which may be empty -- when it does). `regex_match` stays a 0/1 Int (it
is a plain substring test with no sentinel), and the replace helpers keep their
String return (no-match leaves the input unchanged).

Byte offset of the first match as `Int?` -- present holding the offset (which
may legitimately be 0) when the pattern matches, absent when there is no match.
Unwrap with `else -1` to recover the old sentinel view.
